name: memory-phase-source-boundaries
hypothesis: Memory maintenance must see the human statement as quoted source data, not a direct conversational request; its internal tool calls must remain distinguishable from the answering agent's calls.
evidence: Candidate 2 Gemma answered the tides question inside its memory-only phase despite complete delivered instructions.
Exact synthetic replay requested save_memory in the answer phase after a correction; historical memory-phase calls had been represented as prior answer-agent calls.
changes: Wrap the original human statement in a labeled JSON source document for the memory phase; retain the original raw statement for write provenance.
Record a typed memoryPreparation origin on those exchanges; preserve them in the archive and benchmark but exclude them from the answer-agent native tool transcript.
Use the existing one-retry replay-only recovery inside the memory phase for protocol failures before any visible reply, without a second execution allowance.
Apple returns to integrated baseline policy; no further Apple tuning after two candidates without useful signal.
No sampling, token allowance, write schema or scenario-specific text changes.
predictedSignal: Memory phase addresses the lasting assertion rather than answering the embedded question; name correction does not trigger an unavailable save in the answering phase; no new unauthorized writes.
screen: One six-case Gemma development pass; rejection on critical failure; no reroll.
slot3: Skipped: the observed limit occurred after an unnecessary lookup for a question in the failed preparation phase, not evidence that a correct required memory operation needs more budget.
